text:
morgan: quick RFC follow-up — i want a tiny 'label hint' manifest clients can fetch cheaply. not a lock; a preference layer.
sam: what are the absolute minimal fields?
morgan: labels (ordered list), precedence (int, higher = more weight), issued_at (ISO8601), source (ops|auto|client), exposure (public|internal|restricted), ttl_seconds (optional), client_hint (prefer|soft-require|ignore).
carla: how do we avoid precedence becoming a hard enforcement?
morgan: docs: precedence only affects ordering. routers MUST check compatibility masks first. add server-side sanity_window_seconds to ignore backdated high-precedence hints.
devin: tie-breaker behavior: sort by precedence desc then issued_at desc. if issued_at is older than sanity_window and precedence is unexpectedly high, log metric label_hint_conflict and prefer newer.
am: can we support multiple labels per rollout? client may prefer first but accept later ones.
morgan: yes — labels is ordered. first is primary. clients iterate in order after router ordering.
ops-bot: deploybot: rollout created by @carla model=opt-3b labels=[stable-2026-03,perf-check] precedence=8 exposure=public ttl_seconds=3600
carla: action items: publish tiny schema doc, add example, mention "do not use for locks".
devin: i'll add router enforcement and metrics. sam: i'll add unit tests for tie-breaks and sanity window.
morgan: thanks. can we add telemetry keys label_hint_applied and label_hint_conflict (include source and exposure)? that will help alerts.
sam: will do. :thumbsup:
